charge_port.notes: Launches with CCS (TechCrunch, relaying Cadillac); GM moved to NACS only for 2027 (autoevolution). Canadian car assumed the same. Canada: no Canadian page read; assumed the same as the US car (owner check).

supercharger_access.notes: Estimated: GM says every GM EV of model year 2026 or earlier except the Optiq needs the GM NACS adapter (US page, lists Escalade IQ and IQL). Canada: GM sells the same C$310 adapter for its CCS1 EVs (Guide Auto names Lyriq, not the Escalade IQ), so the Canadian car is assumed the same. Model year 2025. Canada: no Canadian page read; assumed the same as the US car (owner check).

ac_max_kw.notes: Luxury 1 has the 11.5 kW onboard charger (Cars.com, US). Edmunds says 19.2 kW is optional on these trims. Canada not stated.

range_km.notes: GM: "Cadillac-estimated 460 miles". Launch figure was 450 miles (TechCrunch, InsideEVs). Canada: "over 700 km" (Auto123, relaying Cadillac); no Canadian per-trim or per-wheel figure found. GM publishes one figure per model, not per wheel size; 24-inch wheels with 35-inch tires were the launch configuration. Manufacturer estimate, not an EPA/NRCan rating (B97).
